name: breather
description: Martin Gardner's minichess (chess on a 5x5 board, each side a rook, knight, bishop, queen and king behind five pawns) played in rounds: both players choose a move in secret, both moves are made together, and a king is simply taken, with no check. What turns the guessing into a game is the breather: the piece that made a side's move sits out that side's next move, unless it is the only piece that can move. No piece can strike twice running, so every attack gives a round's warning, and a king that runs one round has to stand the next, so it must run where no enemy piece free to move can reach it. Each round is a read of the other player: what of theirs can move against your king, and has their king just run, so that it must stand? Striking back is no answer, because two pieces that try to take each other in the same round collide and both die, kings included. If both kings fall together, or the game runs too long, the side with more material left wins.

provenance.history: S4, the candidate game: Gardner in rounds with all three of schema 27's switches against the royal chase (rest, swap collision, both score) and rules.scoring material. Pre-registered in docs/archive/plan-round-chase.md section 5 before it was measured; the study and its grades are there. Joined the library from preview by Q934 (2026-10-17): the library's first royal game played in rounds, Gardner's board and army played in rounds rather than by turns and made decisive (0.971 of games) by the three switches together; viable 4-0 at 0.514. The rest alone (gardner in rounds resting) stayed a preview beside it, as the contrast, until Q962c (2026-10-19) retired it as a near copy of this game. Renamed by Q962 (2026-10-18) from gardner in rounds against the chase (file gardner-in-rounds-against-the-chase.json) to breather, with a description that says what the game is in its own terms rather than against the chase, a preview's problem most visitors never saw; the mechanics and the hash are unchanged.
